title: Latency-budgeted fragmenter for streaming completions (continuous batching + KV residency)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement a new batch-formation heuristic ("Latency-budgeted Fragmenter") tuned for streaming chat completions that jointly reasons about per-request latency budgets, KV cache residency pressure, and GPU memory headroom. This ticket covers design, a small spike implementation in the streaming orchestrator, and an initial canary rollout with synthetic and customer-like traces.

Context and motivation:
- Current continuous batching aggressively coalesces streaming turns which improves throughput but creates high P95 latency spikes when long-history KV lookups cause GPU memory churn.
- We need a heuristic that: respects per-request SLAs (remaining latency budget), avoids reactive thrashing of KV pages into GPU memory, and keeps batch sizes stable across short bursts without starving high-priority traffic.

High-level approach:
1) Maintain a compact per-session "latency_budget" estimate = user SLA - elapsed_time - safety_margin. Use it as the primary admission filter.
2) Predict expected generation length (tokens_remaining) using recent session statistics and a small lightweight estimator; use this to estimate per-request GPU residency cost (kv_pages_needed * bytes_per_page + predicted_decode_temp).
3) Group incoming streaming turns into "fragments" rather than fixed batches: fragments are soft groups bounded by total_estimated_residency and a latency_budget_quantile threshold. Fragments can be flush-triggered by (a) near-deadline requests, (b) residency exceeding soft_slab_reserve, or (c) max_fragment_age.
4) KV residency management: prefer proactive pinning for hot KV slices (recently accessed across many sessions) and opportunistic prefetch for imminent fragments using async DMA copies. When residency pressure is high, prefer evict-on-encode for low-priority or long-LRU slices instead of evicting slices referenced by in-flight fragments.
5) GPU memory accounting: use a two-tier budget model: global slab_reserve (percent of GPU mem for system) + fragment_soft_quota. The fragmenter rejects or routes to fallback (short-seq/CPU) when fragment_soft_quota would exceed available headroom.
6) Fairness and priority: apply a decayed priority score to sessions so high-frequency short-turn users do not monopolize batch slots; provide a priority override for enterprise SLA customers.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Conservative admission reduces throughput; we favor predictable P95 latency for streaming chat over absolute throughput.
- Prefetching KV pages reduces tail latency but increases memory churn and bandwidth; we implement adaptive prefetch with a measured success rate threshold.
- Evict-on-encode avoids large pre-encode residency but may increase decode time if pages must be pulled synchronously; we limit evict-on-encode to low-priority fragments.

Deliverables in this ticket:
- Spec and simulator that takes historic trace and simulates the fragmenter decisions (attached link).
- Minimal orchestrator change: fragmenter module + GPU residency accounting hooks + a config flag to enable on canary.
- Canary rollout plan + dashboards and regression tests.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/FRAG-2025/Latency+Budgeted+Fragmenter
- Spike notebook with trace replay and simulator: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/frag-spike-2025
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/stream-fragmenter/frag-canary-2025
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency on streaming chat workload reduces by >= 25% vs baseline under mixed load (short and long-history sessions) on canary cluster
No increase in token-cost by more than 5% at steady-state throughput
GPU memory OOMs prevented on canary for 48h under synthetic peak replay
Feature gated and togglable per-cluster; rollout-defined telemetry emitted: fragment_size_histogram, fragment_reject_rate, kv_prefetch_success, eviction_count_by_policy
test_plan: Unit tests for fragmenter decision logic (deadline handling, soft_quota enforcement)
Simulator-based regression: run 3 representative traces (short-turn-heavy, long-history-heavy, mixed) and compare against current batching logic
End-to-end canary: enable on a small percentage of runtime nodes and run replay for 72h while monitoring P50/P95/P99 and GPU memory metrics
Failure scenarios: ensure fallback to short-seq model and CPU path when fragmenter rejects due to residency constraints
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dev cluster A/B test with feature flag (1 node) - validate logic and logging
Phase 1: canary on 2% of production inference fleet for 72h - monitor dashboards and SLOs
Phase 2: progressive ramp to 20% with automatic rollback on regression gates (p95 > baseline * 1.15 or memory OOMs)
Phase 3: full rollout with config tuning window and ops runbook updates
notes: We should coordinate with Autoscaling team to make sure slab_reserve signals are visible to cluster scaler
Consider exposing per-customer priority override via Console (requires PM + Console UX work) - separate ticket
If prefetch bandwidth causes PCIe saturation, backoff aggressively and prefer CPU fallback
